paragraphs.english: He visited the town archive with his teacher. An old newspaper showed a photograph of children playing on an unfinished field. title: 絵のついた昼食メニュー

paragraphs.english: At the beginning of the school year, students from several countries joined a lunch club. Each Friday, the members ordered meals from a small restaurant. Some students did not eat meat, and others preferred food without hot peppers. The restaurant had many choices, but its menu used words that new members did not know. Asking a friend to explain every dish took a long time. The club leader, Lisa, wanted everyone to choose a meal without feeling embarrassed. [1] She asked the restaurant owner to check each drawing before printing the new menu. A leaf showed meals without meat, and a pepper showed hot dishes. The pictures did not replace the names or descriptions. They helped students decide which descriptions to read carefully. At the next meeting, ordering took less time, and two new members asked questions about dishes they had never tried. Lisa realized that a small change in information could make joining a group easier.
paragraphs.translation: 新学年、さまざまな国の生徒が昼食クラブに入った。金曜日ごとに小さな飲食店から注文したが、肉を食べない人や辛くない料理を好む人がいた。メニューは選択肢が多くても、新しい部員には分からない語があり、友達に全部説明してもらうのは時間がかかった。リサは恥ずかしがらず選べるよう、料理名の横に簡単な絵を加えることを提案した。印刷前に店主に確認してもらい、葉は肉なし、唐辛子は辛い料理を示した。絵は名前や説明を置き換えるものではなく、詳しく読む説明を選ぶ助けになった。次の会では注文が早くなり、新入部員二人が未経験の料理について質問した。小さな情報の工夫が参加しやすさにつながるとリサは気づいた。
